enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule: Sections 148–151 define bailment and delivery to a bailee, impose the bailor’s duty to disclose known material faults, and require the bailee to take the care that an ordinarily prudent person would take of comparable goods.

Definition: Bailment is delivery of goods for a purpose on an agreement that they will be returned or dealt with according to the bailor’s directions.

Ingredients:
1. Identify bailor, bailee and goods.
2. Establish delivery or legally effective transfer of possession.
3. Identify the purpose and agreed disposition.
4. Apply section 150 disclosure duties and section 151’s standard of care.
examples: A lends B a horse known by A to be vicious without disclosure; B is injured when the horse runs away. The statutory illustration under section 150 makes A responsible for the resulting damage.
problemApplication: Apply sections 148–151: identify the bailment or pledge, test the statutory duty/right, address the relevant exception, and conclude with the legal consequence.
keyTakeaways: Sections 148–151 define bailment and delivery to a bailee, impose the bailor’s duty to disclose known material faults, and require the bailee to take the care that an ordinarily prudent person would take of comparable goods.
Bailment is delivery of goods for a purpose on an agreement that they will be returned or dealt with according to the bailor’s directions.
